gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Noto Sans Chakma packs its lowercase up toward the capitals, with open, uncrowded mouths on the s and c. Azonix supplies the authority, wide-mouthed and crisp when shrunk.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-cham: Tight-knit and commanding, Azonix writes with one steady pen pressure from first letter to last. Noto Sans Cham brings tall, rounded lowercase and a generous entry into every c.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Hard-edged, uniform and imposing, Azonix draws every line alike. Azonix does its best work announcing, with wide mouths that stay crisp small, while Noto Sans Cherokee quietly carries text with its tall band of letters.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Commanding and unmodulated, Azonix holds every line at one gauge. Noto Sans Cuneiform, with its open e and inflated, bead-like lowercase, would read smoothly and comfortably line after line.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Azonix looks like bent tubing, the same gauge from end to end. Noto Sans Duployan has a wide-mouthed a and oversized counters, which would sprawl if the body text were enlarged.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Letters that look bent from a single wire give Azonix its look, while Noto Sans Georgian keeps open curves throughout. Azonix earns its keep when it is big and brief.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Azonix has no thick-thin shift at all, like an outline of steel cable, with wide mouths that stay crisp. It commands; Noto Sans Gujarati, with large open counters, simply reads.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Authoritative and tubelike, Azonix holds a constant weight, while Noto Sans Hebrew lets a dominant midsection swallow the line's height. Azonix announces while the sans body simply gets on with reading.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Wire-bent and commanding, Azonix sets capitals only slightly above its lowercase. Noto Sans Kannada is gentler, with a soft bump up to capitals and s curves open wide at both ends.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kharoshth: Azonix has stroke contrast of exactly none, and its wide-mouthed letters stay crisp when shrunk. Noto Sans Kharoshthi, with curves that never close and a dark stripe of lowercase, holds a steady rhythm down the page.
